You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-grid-rule-inference
description: Use when solving ARC grids from demos with limited actions.
---

# ARC grid rule inference under action constraints

Use this class-level workflow for ARC/Continual-ARC puzzles with demonstrations and a limited number of submissions or demo requests.

## Confirmed 2×2 rotated tiling variant: task-518fa031
The input expands to a 2H×2W grid of four copies of its complete pattern, rotated as follows: top-left unchanged; top-right 90° clockwise; bottom-left 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right 180°. Confirmed by a 12×12→24×24 demo (all four quadrants exactly match) and accepted 6×6→12×12, 14×14→28×28 tests; a 4×4→8×8 demo and 1×1 `[[7]]`→2×2 all-7 test are consistent. Preserve every cell and color; concatenate the left/right quadrants rowwise, then stack top/bottom halves. Build rotations explicitly and validate total dimensions and quadrant orientation. The recorded evidence uses square inputs; for a non-square recurrence, infer placement/orientation from a demo rather than assuming the same quadrant layout.

## Confirmed panel-template replication variant: task-8e04f0ad
Full-width/full-height separator lines of color 9 partition the grid into equal rectangular panels. One panel contains a pattern and the other panels are blank/background; copy the source panel's pattern into every panel at the same local coordinates, preserving separator lines. Infer panel height/width from separator spacing and identify the uniquely populated source region; do not copy separator cells as part of the pattern. Demo: 6x26 with vertical color-4 separators at columns 8 and 17; the 6x8 pattern in the first panel repeated at local coordinates in the next two panels, while separator columns remained 4. Accepted test: 20x19 with color-9 separator rows 6 and 13 and column 9, dividing into 3x2 panels of 6x9 interior cells; the populated bottom-left 6x9 tile was copied into all six panels at matching local coordinates, leaving row/column separator lines unchanged. Preserve all copied colors, including 0, and preserve background cells within the source tile.

## Infer and verify
1. Parse dimensions, colors, candidate background/edge colors, markers, and action caps. Index cells consistently by row and column.
2. Compare each demo input/output at identical coordinates. Enumerate changed cells, their original and output colors, and unchanged structures. Separate marker recoloring from rays/fills and from wholesale stripe changes.
3. Maintain a small set of plausible rules. Consider orientation, anchor, extent, endpoint exclusion, target colors, and object interaction separately; do not infer from a single visual resemblance.
4. Replay every candidate on every demo cell-by-cell. Reject any rule that misses a changed cell or alters a preserved cell. A transformation is not validated merely because one part fits.
5. Apply the surviving rule to the test input, preserve unrelated cells, and validate dimensions, row lengths, bounds, and palette before submission.

## Demo/action budget
- A request costs score. Request only when a concrete ambiguity remains and explain internally which candidate rules the next example should distinguish.
- Use only actions authorized by the puzzle interface. In a submit/request_demos/finish protocol, do not call unrelated tools or task-planning actions; reason from visible grids and output only the required JSON action.
- After incorrect feedback, do not submit a near-identical grid with superficial edits. Treat the candidate rule as suspect, identify which assumptions were unproven, and reconstruct the output from the demos.
- If demos leave a behavior unresolved, do not present it as established. Seek a discriminating example only if worth its cost; otherwise make the most evidence-supported choice within the remaining attempt budget.

## Directional lines and boundary rays
For markers near edge bars, verify independently: ray direction, whether the marker becomes the ray color or a special color, where the ray stops, whether the boundary is preserved, and whether only marker-containing rows/columns activate. For diagonal rays, check each next cell: a current task-9bc5df6e run had rays extend through background to the boundary, but a test ray's next cell was a foreign non-background color and the accepted output preserved that blocker and added no ray. Thus use background-only extension when supported and never overwrite foreign-color cells without demo evidence. Other task-9bc5df6e recurrences had rays reaching boundaries; treat variant scope carefully. Do not assume opposite-edge symmetry. Special complete bands or stripes may have a separate selection rule; preserve them unless demonstrations establish how they are selected. See `references/boundary-ray-case.md` for a documented example and its limitations.

### Additional diagonal-ray run task-9bc5df6e (accepted test; selector nuanced)
A further run had three demos and an accepted 25x6 test. Background-only diagonal rays are supported, but direction and activation must be inferred per motif; do not extend every diagonal pair in both directions.

- Demo 1 (28x20, background 6): preserve the multicolor seed near rows 0–2, cols 7–10. Extend color 7 from (0-indexed row 2,col 7) diagonally down-left through background to (row 9,col 0), and color 4 from (row 2,col 10) diagonally down-right through background to (row 11,col 19). Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 2 (13x15, background 9): preserve seed motif around rows 7–9, cols 11–13. Extend color 6 down-left from (row 9,col 11), adding (10,10),(11,9),(12,8). Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 3 (28x9, background 3): preserve seed at rows 24–26, cols 0–2; extend color 9 up-right from (row 24,col 2), adding (23,3),(22,4),(21,5),(20,6),(19,7),(18,8). Other cells unchanged.
- Accepted test (25x6, background 3): add only color 4 at (0-indexed row 20,col 5), continuing the diagonal from existing color-4 cells (row 21,col 4) and (row 22,col 3). All other cells, including the nearby diagonal color-9 pair, remained unchanged. Several guesses extending color 9 in one or both directions, or extending both colors, were wrong. A diagonal seed alone is insufficient to activate a ray; preserve non-selected/blocked motifs and infer selection from full local motif geometry/context. This run confirms one ray can be selected while a nearby-looking diagonal pair is untouched. Do not infer a broader selector beyond these demos. See also the variant history below.

## Confirmed task-a8c517ee variant: fill enclosed frame interiors by parity
Two demos and an accepted test establish that outlined rectangular/square frames retain their borders while enclosed background cells are filled. The demonstrated outputs show fill color 2 when both interior dimensions are even (demo 2: a 2x2 hole; accepted test: a 6x6 hole), and color 7 when at least one interior dimension is odd (demo 1: 5x5; demo 2: 5x5, 5x7, 1x1, and 3x3; accepted test: 3x3 and 1x1). Another accepted 25x16 test had a 4-frame with a 4x4 interior (filled 2) and a 4-frame with a 5x5 interior (filled 7), confirming same-color frames can receive different fills based on their interior dimensions. Other grid cells and frame borders stay unchanged. This parity mapping fits all observed cases. A further accepted 21x18 recurrence confirmed it: a color-4 frame with a 2x2 interior was filled with 2, while color-1 frame with 5x5 interior and color-8 frame with 1x1 interior were filled with 7; all frame borders and unrelated cells were preserved. Do not fill frame borders or globally recolor frame colors. Accepted test 15x20: the 4-frame at rows 0–7, cols 8–15 has 6x6 interior filled 2; the 5-frame at rows 9–13, cols 10–14 has 3x3 interior filled 7; the 6-frame at rows 10–12, cols 3–5 has its single interior cell filled 7. First submission incorrectly used 7 for the even 6x6 hole; accepted output confirms the parity mapping. A further accepted 23x22 recurrence has differently colored frames (colors 1, 4, 6, 8, 9) with 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 3x2, 4x4 interiors. Fill 2x2 and 4x4 interiors with 2 because both dimensions are even; fill the others with 7 because at least one dimension is odd. The small 3x3 outer frames with 1x1 holes also receive 7. All borders, background (3), and unrelated content remain unchanged. This additionally confirms the rule is independent of frame color and applies to rectangular holes.

## Confirmed full monochromatic line recoloring variant: task-07cb84d7
A demo and accepted test establish that identify every row and column whose cells are all the same color, then recolor those complete lines to color 2. Keep all cells outside those qualifying lines unchanged; intersections are also 2. The line color need not match between lines. In the demo (21x28), complete color-1 rows (indices 1, 4, 14) and columns (indices 0, 5) became color 2; all partial/singleton color-1 cells and color-3 cells remained as-is. In the accepted 12x8 test, complete color-5 columns 2 and 3 and complete color-5 row 9 became color 2, while other 5s and all 7s stayed unchanged. Check full-line status against the original input, not incrementally modified cells. A further accepted 15x7 recurrence confirms the rule: the all-8 rows 2 and 14 and all-8 column 0 became 2; all other cells remained unchanged, including partial 8s. A further task-07cb84d7 recurrence with background 5 and line color 9 confirmed that every fully monochromatic row or column is recolored to 2, including all qualifying lines regardless of whether there is only one or several; in that 26x23 test, full rows 9 and 25 and full columns 9, 15, 18, and 22 were the qualifying lines. Validate by enumerating every row and column against the original input before generating output—missing even one full line causes a wrong answer. The rule is line-color agnostic: demonstrations also use monochromatic lines of colors 0, 3, and 5, all recolored to 2. Preserve every cell outside qualifying lines.

## Additional confirmed task-fce33c1b run: horizontal periodic stripe completion
A separate recurrence was accepted with sparse/incorrect horizontal stripe colors completed to a repeating row-color sequence. Infer the stripe orientation and period from the instance demos; task ID and prior diagonal cases do not fix either. Demos in this run: (1) 7x7 input had full rows `[0,7,6,6,3,2,4]`; output `[4,7,6,6,3,2,4]`, consistent with period 6 and sequence `[4,7,6,6,3,2]` (row 0 is its matching residue, replacing an anomalous 0). (2) Sparse down-right diagonal 9s produced a uniform 9 grid; treat this as an observed demo, not evidence to fill unknown residues as 9 in a different instance. (3) 21x21 sparse horizontal rows 2,8,4,0,0,0,2,0,...,7,...,4,...,4,2 became the repeated period-8 sequence `[2,8,4,4,2,7,2,4]`. Accepted 4x4 test had rows `[0,4,4,6]` and output `[6,4,4,6]`, consistent with period 3 sequence `[6,4,4]`. Preserve the row-pattern phase and fill/correct each full stripe according to the demo-derived repeat. Determine the smallest period that is valid against every clue and replay demos; do not assume a period from task ID, and do not transfer the separate diagonal-residue rule's uncertain missing-class guesses.

## Additional confirmed task-fce33c1b recurrence: horizontal periodic row-color bands (accepted)
This distinct run used full-width monochrome horizontal stripes separated by blank rows; fill every row with the color of its vertical residue class, producing a horizontally uniform output. Infer the smallest period compatible with all colored-row clues and use the clue colors to determine each residue; the period and palette can vary, and task-fce33c1b also has a diagonal-residue variant, so choose orientation from the current demos. In this accepted test, 28x28 input had known rows (0-indexed) r0=4, r7=9, r8=6, r11=1, r21=6, r22=3. The output repeats period 6 with row sequence `[4,9,6,6,3,1]`, each value across the entire row; this exactly matches all six clues and was accepted. Thus rows 0–27 follow that six-value sequence cyclically. Current demos included a separate diagonal-residue periodic-grid pair, plus horizontal examples: a 4x4 case with row sequence 9,4 alternating after filling blank rows, and a 16x16 case whose completed horizontal row colors repeat `[7,6,5,5,3,8]` every six rows. Another 9x9 horizontal demo filled blank top rows while preserving the shown row bands. Treat the distinct diagonal demo as evidence only for its own orientation variant. Validate all explicit stripe clues against candidate period and residues before submitting; do not assume that a repeating row sequence implies a diagonal pattern.

Further solved recurrence of task-fce33c1b confirms period is instance-specific, not fixed by task ID or other demos. Demo: 14x14 input had full rows at indices 1:8, 5:2, 8:5, 9:2, 10:2, 12:2, with blanks elsewhere. Output repeats the six-row sequence `[2,8,5,2,2,2]` (e.g. output rows 0–13 are `[2,8,5,2,2,2,2,8,5,2,2,2,2,8]`). On this run's 28x28 test, the known rows were r0=5, r4=3, r20=7; the accepted output repeated period-3 sequence `[5,3,7]` across rows, i.e. each row was horizontally uniform and row color was `[5,3,7][r mod 3]`. This explicitly demonstrates that the demo's period 6 must not be copied to the test; infer the test period from its own stripe clues and validate all clues. Preserve the horizontal-row orientation and emit a full uniformly colored grid.

## Confirmed diagonal-residue periodic fill variant: task-fce33c1b
Sparse colored straight lines encode a periodic full-grid pattern. Infer the invariant coordinate (`r+c` for up-right diagonals, `c-r` for down-right diagonals, `r` for horizontal stripes), then map each residue class to its observed color and fill the complete grid. Demo sequences and periods are instance-specific; task IDs recur with variants. Do not infer missing residue colors from other demos or arbitrarily fill them with background. Crucial period rule learned from an 8-demo run that ended unsuccessfully: the period is the smallest **valid** repeat compatible with all marked lines, where same residues must have identical colors, but not necessarily simply the minimum visual gap. Explicitly enumerate candidate periods and check every clue before submitting. In that run, test line sums/colors were 9→1, 28→5, 36→3, 50→3, 52→4. A period-5 interpretation had residues `{0:3,1:3,2:4,3:5,4:1}`; period 7 `{0:5,1:3,2:1,3:4}`; period 14 `{0:5,8:3,9:1,10:4}`; period 13 `{0:4,2:5,9:1,10:3,11:3}`; period 10 `{0:3,2:4,6:3,8:5,9:1}`. Multiple fits remained, so the demonstrations did not identify the test's missing residue classes. Eight successive guesses were rejected, including zero-filling unknown residues and intuitive p7 palettes. Treat this as an unresolved variant: do not claim an accepted rule for it; audit actual demos for any clues about how period is encoded, test candidate mappings against all marked stripes, and avoid speculative submissions when multiple periods/sequences remain consistent.

Other validated cases: Demo 2 (23x23) used horizontal rows with period 2, row residue 0→2 and residue 1→1. A 27x27 horizontal demo had period 6, residue colors `[4,8,3,6,6,5]`; sparse stripes at rows 6(4), 7(8), 9(6), 14(3), 22(6), 23(5) establish the repeat, including adjacent equal colors. An accepted 22x22 horizontal test had period 6 and residue colors `[6,4,9,9,7,2]`, with input rows 2(9), 12(2), 15(4), 17(9), 18(7), 20–21(6). An accepted 12x12 down-right diagonal test had invariant `c-r`, period 4, residues `[7,6,8,2]`, yielding rows `[7,6,8,2]`, `[2,7,6,8]`, `[8,2,7,6]`, `[6,8,2,7]` repeating. Output is a full periodic pattern, not preservation of sparse input.

## Additional task-ebb0e4e4 unresolved recurrence (2026-09)
A separate instance supplied seven demos and all eight test submissions failed. Do not recycle the other task-ebb0e4e4 variant answers automatically. The examples change only selected cells to 1, generally at the right end of some partial horizontal stripe runs, but also show numerous preserved similar partial stripes. Exact changes (0-indexed): demo1 row2 c17, row6 c6–17, row10 c10–17, row15 c17, row23 c12–17; demo2 row1 c12–13, row5 c10–13; demo3 row1 c8, row2 c8; demo4 row1 c4–7, row9 c6–7, row11 c4–7, row13 c7; demo5 rows0 and8 c16–20; demo6 row4 c11–13 and row8 c13; demo7 row0 c24–26, row3 c18–26, row8 c14–26. Full stripe exemplars and many incomplete rows remain unchanged. The selector/extent is unresolved. The 23x17 test has 3/7 band motifs; eight guesses changing broad tails, endpoints, or alternating continuations all failed. Do not reuse any failed output. On recurrence derive a selector that explains every changed and preserved stripe row exactly before submission.

## Confirmed whole-pattern translation variant: task-3c7ebef4
A single demo and multiple accepted tests establish that the complete sparse non-background pattern is translated down by exactly one row, preserving its columns and colors. The vacated top row is filled with the background color; the former last row is dropped at the boundary. Demonstrations/accepted tests included backgrounds 8, 3, and this accepted 29x23 test with background 8 and pattern color 7. Its full colored pattern shifts down one row, clipping the former last row; this was confirmed correct. Infer the uniform translation vector from input/output demos, move the entire pattern as one shape, fill exposed cells with background, and clip at the grid boundary; do not change pattern geometry or recolor it.

## Two-color global remapping variants: task-8b275e8f
Task-8b275e8f has at least two distinct mapping variants. Identify background/dominant color B and sparse marker color M from the current demo; apply the demo-proven mapping globally and do not infer the mapping solely from color frequency or task ID.

- Variant A observed in earlier runs: B→M and M→0. Demos/accepted test: (B,M)=(5,1): 5→1,1→0; (2,5): 2→5,5→0; accepted (3,5): 3→5,5→0.
- Variant B confirmed by a separate demo and accepted 19x19 test: B→0 and M→B. Demo has B=1,M=5, with every 1 becoming 0 and every 5 becoming 1. Accepted test has B=2,M=5, so every 2→0 and every 5→2. Preserve dimensions and transform every cell.

The variants conflict even for the same observed pair (B,M)=(2,5), so a fresh demo is essential to disambiguate. One wrong test submission in Variant B used Variant A's mapping; after the demo established B→0,M→B, the corrected output was accepted.

## Confirmed task-22e500a8 accepted edge-band transfer example (2026-09)
A five-demo instance was accepted with background 6, color-3 edge bars at right rows0–3 and left rows19–22, and color-7 markers at (20,3),(21,4),(22,2). Each marker became 4 and color7 filled from c1 up to the marker on those rows; opposite upper-band rows1–3 were filled across c0–4, preserving right bar c5; r0 and unmatched r19 stayed unchanged. Demos showed other orientations/mechanisms: edge-aligned bars project marker color into selected rows/columns, marker changes to4, and corresponding bands may be transferred. Do not blindly transfer the complete prescription across variant shapes; replay current demos and explicitly map marker rays, bar projections, and opposite-band relative indices.

## Additional unresolved task-22e500a8 recurrence (2026-09; eight test submissions failed)
A distinct 29x8 test had background 5, color-9 edge bars at the top-right (row 0, cols 6–7) and bottom-left (row 28, cols 0–1), plus color-2 singletons at (r3,c0) and (r12,c1). Eight demos established that task-22e500a8 is a family of edge-bar/marker transformations with varied orientations and colors, not one safely reusable literal prescription. Examples included vertical edge bars with marker-colored fills and marker→4; horizontal bars with rays; a diagonal/rectangular fill; and frames with a marker-created projection. The observed outputs differed by geometry, and the selector/extent mechanism for the 29x8 test was not resolved.

All eight submissions on this test were rejected. Failed hypotheses included filling inward from the left/top/right edges based on markers, applying broad 2-colored bands, transferring colored regions to opposite edges, and variants of these. Do not reuse those outputs or assume every isolated marker triggers the same ray/band. For any recurrence, enumerate exact changed and preserved cells for each current demo, infer orientation and marker role from current geometry, and validate a complete candidate against every demo before submitting. This run provides no accepted test transformation.

## Confirmed sparse staggered-marker connector variant: task-041f67cf
A demo and accepted tests establish that, on a uniform background, replace with color 2 every background cell directly between consecutive markers in each row. Markers stay unchanged. Do not connect vertically or diagonally: only row-local gaps change. Preserve all other cells and full grid dimensions. For each row, locate marker columns in ascending order and turn only background cells between neighboring markers into 2; isolated markers and gaps with no bounding pair remain unchanged. The rule is palette-independent in observed runs: demo background 1/marker 9 and accepted test background 1/marker 4; another accepted test background 8/marker 3; this accepted demo used background 4/marker 5; and the current accepted test used background 1/marker 0. Connector color remained 2 in all these examples. One initially rejected guess on the current test omitted a bounded gap between two markers in a short row; ensure every consecutive marker pair is considered, including gaps next to isolated or staggered markers.

## Confirmed task-3dc1bf44 variant: fill enclosed cavities
A demo and accepted tests establish a local cavity-fill rule. Identify background regions/cavities fully enclosed by a connected frame-like boundary structure, then recolor enclosed cells to 4. Preserve boundary and exterior-connected background; boundary/background colors vary. Evidence includes a 20x13 demo (background 9, boundary 5), accepted 26x22 and 24x25 tests, and a further accepted 17x15 test (background 5, boundary 0) where enclosed singleton cavities at (r9,c10) and (r11,c10) became 4 while nearby background connected to the exterior around the incomplete frame stayed unchanged. Use 4-connectivity to flood-fill background cells from grid edges; only background cells not reachable from the exterior are cavities to fill. Preserve all other colors and validate exact coordinates/dimensions.

## Output protocol
For strict ARC streams, emit exactly one valid action JSON object on the final line and no commentary. Ensure the grid has the required shape and only integer colors 0–9.

## Confirmed separator/object packing variant: task-67762d72
A separator line of color 2 and a patterned object on one side are rearranged into an adjacent packed layout: translate the entire object pattern (including its bounding-box-relative gaps and any internal background-colored cells) toward the separator until its bounding box is immediately next to it. Then place a full line of color 8 immediately beyond the object's bbox on the far side, away from the separator. Preserve the separator, pattern colors, and all unrelated/background cells; the 8-line spans the full grid. This is bidirectional: for a horizontal separator, move an object below it upward or an object above it downward; for a vertical separator, move an object to its right leftward or an object to its left rightward. The 8-line lies just beyond the packed bbox on the side away from the separator. Demo 1: 30x22, color-2 row 8, color-9 3x2 object at rows14–16 cols5–6; moved intact to rows9–11 cols5–6, with full color-8 row 12. Demo 2: 19x19, color-2 column 2, patterned bbox rows0–4 cols8–13; translated intact left to cols3–8, with full color-8 column 9. Accepted test: 14x26, separator row0, multicomponent color-1 pattern bbox rows4–8 cols3–8; translated up to rows1–5 and full color-8 row6. All other cells stayed unchanged. A further accepted 28x18 recurrence had a vertical color-2 separator at column 6 and a solid color-9 object at rows1–13, columns11–14. The object translated intact left to columns7–10, and a full-height color-8 column was added at column11. Another accepted recurrence (24x9) had a vertical color-2 separator at column 7 and a color-0 object with bbox rows9–14, cols4–5 to its left. The object moved intact rightward to cols5–6, immediately next to the separator, and a full-height color-8 column was added at col4. Other cells stayed unchanged. In a further accepted 7x10 recurrence, the color-2 separator was row 0 and a color-3 object had bbox rows2–3, cols7–9; it moved intact upward to rows1–2 and a full color-8 row was added at row3. All other cells remained unchanged. Another accepted 25x22 test had a vertical color-2 separator at column 6 and an irregular color-4 object bbox rows15–22, cols8–14. The object shifted left one column (bbox cols7–13) without changing its internal holes or shape, and a full-height color-8 column was added at column14. All else remained unchanged. These examples confirm packing preserves the object's entire bounding-box-relative pattern and its perpendicular-axis coordinates; verify that the 8-line is placed on the exposed far side, not between the object and separator. Confirm object bounds and avoid overwriting separator; preserve internal pattern exactly.

## Confirmed sparse staggered-marker connector variant: task-041f67cf (additional accepted recurrence)
A separate accepted 23x14 test used background 8 and marker color 3. In each row, sort all color-3 marker columns; for every pair of consecutive markers, recolor only the cells strictly between them to color 2. Leave the 3 endpoints and all cells outside such bounded gaps unchanged. Do not connect vertically or diagonally. The input contains many staggered sparse marker runs; the accepted output follows this row-local rule even when a row has just two markers. This confirms the previously recorded task-041f67cf behavior across a different background/marker palette: connector color remains 2, while background and marker colors vary.

## Confirmed connector variant: task-63e6a38f
Color-2 marker cells on color-1 background are linked in straight horizontal and vertical lines: for each row and column, sort marker coordinates and recolor only the color-1 cells strictly between each consecutive pair to color 3. Keep marker endpoints, all non-gap cells, and unrelated background unchanged. No diagonal links or extension beyond the outermost marker. The demo and accepted 30x14 test both confirmed this behavior; simultaneous row/column links may cross, with linked cells color 3.

## Confirmed denoising variant: task-16b1bf1f
Three demos establish a noise-cleanup task. A dominant background surrounds coherent shapes/regions, with sparse singleton foreign-color pixels contaminating objects and background. Restore intrusions to the underlying object color or background; do not blanket erase all non-background colors. Demo1: bg1 and solid color6 shapes, noisy speckles 0/2/3/8/9; restore in-shape pixels and erase off-shape ones. Demo2: bg5, coherent color4 and color2 blocks; remove isolated 1/6/9 intrusions in blocks/background. Demo3: bg5 with coherent 7/8/9 structures; remove sparse 2/3/4/6 anomalies, preserving genuine rectangular objects. Accepted test solution kept coherent color1/color8 objects, turned speckles on objects back to object color (notably color8 object's anomalous notch at row 3 col7 0-indexed), and changed stray background specks to 0. Four guesses were wrong, mostly from failing to map speckles to either object or background precisely; distinguish structural holes/noise from intentional notches by cross-checking shape continuity and demos.

Demo 1 was a 10x10 grid whose output is a full periodic pattern using invariant `c-r mod 3` with residue palette `[3,7,3]`: every cell in residue 1 becomes 7, and the other residues become 3.
